name: Lane Marsh
life: “I still remember learning rejection letters had to be signed by hand.” Saturday often includes a stop at the blocks below Foundry Lofts, where Lane checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I am keeping the wrong envelopes for rejection letters. The founder wants to write those by hand.
appearance: Lane has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Look for thick, tightly coiled hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a black overshirt with pearl buttons with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. In conversation Lane turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Lane treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To let the founder sign the hard letters personally.
family: Amanda Quintero is Lane’s cousin. Lane asks before bringing somebody along. Amanda can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The missing name on the stern*, Amanda says, “I make marine flags. I suggested one name on each side so a boat leaving and returning tells the whole story.”
connections: Alexei Gibbs. The instruction preserved by the printer determines which letters the founder will sign.

reactions.situation: The founder is asked to use a formal name
reactions.response: Lane leaves the founder to decide what her own name on a letter should be.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Lane suggests breakfast together and lets the offer rest until another day.
